sleepium.ui.title: Sleepium settings
sleepium.ui.open.tooltip: Settings of Sleepium: features, shaderpacks, flags
sleepium.ui.reset.tooltip: Every engine flag back to the tested defaults (the shaderpack stays)
sleepium.ui.restart: Restart the game to apply %s change(s)
sleepium.ui.locked: Set by a launch flag (-D%s): change it in the launcher's JVM arguments
sleepium.ui.duplicates: Sleepium: several copies in the mods folder (%s). The game uses %s - delete the others.
sleepium.ui.hud.on.tip: Sleepium's HUD in the game's corners: the widgets below, each in the corner you choose. Hidden while F3 is open. It costs next to nothing: data is gathered only for the widgets shown, and the HUD is redrawn a few times a second.
sleepium.ui.hud.rate.tip: How often the HUD's numbers are redrawn; in between the last drawing is shown again (no text layout per frame).
sleepium.ui.hud.w.fps.tip: FPS and frame times: the median (p50) and the slowest 1 % (p99) of the last 240 frames.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.graph.tip: The last 120 frames as bars: green normal, yellow slower, red a stutter; the violet top of a bar is a GC pause in it; the white line is the median.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.stutters.tip: Frames over twice the median (and 17 ms over it): how many in the last minute and the last one taken apart - the client tick, GC pauses, the rest (drawing, uploads). Each one also goes to logs/sleepium-stutters.log while shown.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.server.tip: The integrated server's time per tick (singleplayer and LAN host): over 50 ms the world slows down.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.gc.tip: GC pauses in the last minute and the last one (the collector, its cause) - from the JVM's own notifications.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.threads.tip: CPU per thread group over the last second, in cores (1.00 = one core busy all the time): which threads do the work.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.memory.tip: The heap used / its maximum and how fast the game allocates (what the GC has to clean).
sleepium.ui.hud.w.mods.tip: The mods whose blocks and mobs cost most right now (the last 3 s): timed where Sleepium calls them. While shown it costs a timestamp per block / mob tick.
sleepium.ui.hud.w.sleep.tip: Block entities asleep / tracked and ticks skipped per second (singleplayer).
sleepium.ui.hud.w.world.tip: F3's entity and chunk lines (drawn / in the level, sections compiled) without opening F3.
sleepium.ui.mods.profile.tip: Measures what each mod costs: its blocks' and mobs' ticks on the server, its mobs' ticks and drawing on the client - timed where Sleepium makes those calls. The screen closes and the game runs for 15 s (play as usual: go where it is slow); a line in the chat says when it is done.
sleepium.ui.mods.profile.done: Sleepium: measured what each mod costs - Options -> Sleepium -> Mods
sleepium.ui.mods.cost.tip: The last measurement (%s): time in its blocks' and mobs' code per server tick, in drawing its mobs per frame.
sleepium.ui.mods.cost.none: Nothing of it was measured (none of its blocks or mobs ticked or were drawn)
sleepium.ui.mods.header: What Sleepium does to each mod
sleepium.ui.mods.export.tip: For modpack makers: writes %s from your choices here (switches that differ from the defaults and the rules per mod). Ship that file with the pack; players can still change what is not locked.
sleepium.ui.mods.untouched: Nothing yet: Sleepium has not changed or put to sleep anything of this mod (its blocks and mobs show up once they tick in a world).
sleepium.ui.mods.what.tip: Filled while the game runs: Sleepium's changes that gave way to this mod, its blocks and mobs as they first tick, and why each one sleeps or not.
sleepium.ui.mods.rule.sleep.tip: Its machines and other block entities: on - they sleep when Sleepium proves them idle; watched - only while watched closely (64 idle ticks first, every owned value compared); off - they always tick.
sleepium.ui.mods.rule.entitySleep.tip: Its mobs and other entities: on - they sleep when idle; off - they always tick.
sleepium.ui.mods.rule.renderCache.tip: Its entities and block entities drawn from Sleepium's render cache when unchanged; off - always drawn the mod's own way.
sleepium.ui.mods.rule.parallelRender.tip: Its entities drawn on Sleepium's helper threads; off - always on the render thread (for renderers that must stay there).
sleepium.ui.mods.rule.giveWay.tip: When Sleepium's change and this mod's change meet in the same code: on a conflict - Sleepium gives way (the default); always - also where they only touch the same method; never - Sleepium's change wins and the mod's conflicting mixin is taken out (the mod may lose that feature: check it). Takes effect after a restart.
sleepium.ui.lockedPack: Set and locked by the modpack (config/sleepium-pack.properties)
sleepium.ui.source.pack: The modpack chose this (config/sleepium-pack.properties); your change overrides it.
sleepium.ui.source.mod: The mod %s asks for this; your change overrides it.
sleepium.ui.shaders.empty: No packs in the shaderpacks folder yet
sleepium.ui.shaders.note: Beta: shaderpacks (OptiFine / Iris format, .zip or folder) are run by Sleepium itself and switch without a restart; the world's chunks are rebuilt. Not every pack feature is supported yet.
sleepium.ui.group.chunks.desc: Chunks drawn in a few multi-draws, packed vertices, mesh and draw memos, render cache.
sleepium.ui.group.entities_render.desc: Entities and block entities drawn in batches, without per-frame garbage.
sleepium.ui.group.lighting.desc: Light updates off the render thread, light scouting, shader-side light.
sleepium.ui.group.animation.desc: GeckoLib models: parallel bone work, compiled Molang, shared keyframes.
sleepium.ui.group.ticks.desc: Sleeping idle mobs, collision and shape memos, neighbour and redstone updates, AI, events.
sleepium.ui.group.threads.desc: Main-thread reactor, parallel entities, reused pools.
sleepium.ui.group.worldgen.desc: Parallel generation, shared noise, work skipped where it cannot change the result.
sleepium.ui.group.saving.desc: Chunk saving and loading off the main thread, chunk caches.
sleepium.shaders.preparing: Sleepium: preparing %s... %s (shaders on when ready; the first time on a driver takes longest)
sleepium.ui.partof.tip: Switched together with %s: click to go there
sleepium.ui.partof.hidden: Needs %s, an experimental part that is switched only by a launch flag (-D%s=true)
sleepium.ui.stats.tip: Live: frame times from the last 240 frames; the server's tick (singleplayer); the sleep engine's block entities asleep now and the ticks it saves each second.
sleepium.ui.stats.sleep: Asleep: %s of %s block entities, %s ticks/s saved
sleepium.ui.presets.tip: Maximum: everything incl. experimental. Recommended: the tested set (the default). Compatible: without the client's rendering parts, for other rendering mods. Off: vanilla.
sleepium.ui.preset.maximum.tip: Every optimisation, including the experimental ones
sleepium.ui.preset.recommended.tip: The tested set every release is checked with
sleepium.ui.preset.compatible.tip: Without terrain, entity and light rendering changes: for use with other rendering mods
sleepium.ui.hud.tip: FPS, frame time p99 and (singleplayer) the server's tick and what sleeps, in the top left corner while playing (hidden with F3).
sleepium.ui.report.label: Report for a bug
sleepium.ui.report.tip: Copies Sleepium's version, the game and Forge versions, the GPU and driver, the shaderpack and every changed flag: paste it into an issue.
sleepium.ui.calibration.tip: Some speed-ups help one machine and cost another, so Sleepium measures them once on your graphics card, driver and mods and remembers the result (config/sleepium-calibration.properties). Recalibrate forgets it: the next seconds of play measure again. Use it after a driver update or when something feels slower than it should.
sleepium.ui.calibration.done: Measuring again - keep playing for a minute
sleepium.ui.hover: Point at something to read what it does.
sleepium.ui.packopts.hint: Click: next value, Shift+click: previous. Point at an option to read the pack's note on it.
sleepium.ui.packopts.unsaved: Changed: Apply or Done saves to shaderpacks/<pack>.txt and prepares the pack again.
